claim: The standard binned ECE estimator (ECE_bin) is statistically biased, with the direction and magnitude of bias depending on the type of model miscalibration, the size of the evaluation dataset, and the number of bins chosen.
stance_target: treating a reported ECE number as an unbiased, protocol-independent ground truth for calibration quality
scope_conditions: general neural network calibration evaluation; validated via synthesized model outputs matching real-network statistics
quoted_support: We instead focus on assessing statistical bias in this empirical measure, and we identify better estimators... We find that binning-based estimators with bins of equal mass (number of instances) have lower bias than estimators with bins of equal width.

claim: Equal-width binning, the conventional default in most calibration papers, produces higher-bias ECE estimates than equal-mass binning.
stance_target: ECE computed with default/unreported equal-width binning as a robust methodological choice
quoted_support: We find that binning-based estimators with bins of equal mass (number of instances) have lower bias than estimators with bins of equal width.

claim: Using debiased calibration-error estimators (the debiased estimator or the proposed ECE_sweep) changes conclusions about the effectiveness of recalibration methods and the detection of model miscalibration compared to conventional ECE_bin.
stance_target: post-hoc calibration methods' reported ECE improvements being robust to the choice of calibration-error estimator
scope_conditions: synthetic and real neural network calibration evaluation settings
quoted_support: With these estimators, we observe improvements in the effectiveness of recalibration methods and in the detection of model miscalibration.
